citation: Yamao Y. (2023) 観測現場発 季節のたより[21] 苫小牧にて (Seasonal letter from the field, Tomakomai). CGER News Vol. 34 No. 4 (No. 392), July 2023
quote: 台風から15年が経過し、シラカンバなどの高木類の生長が顕著になったため、2019年に30ｍのタワーを新設し
note: Translation: '15 years after the typhoon, growth of tall trees such as white birch had become marked, so in 2019 a 30 m tower was newly built'. Check for a flux discontinuity in 2019.

extent_or_severity: about half of Tomakomai Experimental Forest disturbed
effect_on_stand: stand-replacing in much of the forest; present secondary DBF colonised afterwards
citation: Hiura T. (2005) Estimation of aboveground biomass and net biomass increment in a cool temperate forest on a landscape scale. Ecol. Res. 20:271-277
quote: Half the area of TOEF was disturbed by a catastrophic typhoon in 1954
note: Typhoon Toyamaru (named in Hiura et al. 2005 report as 洞爺丸台風). 1954 damage was concentrated in the east of the forest. Read as Springer HTML full text (institutional access); quotes as returned by the fetch tool.

extent_or_severity: forest-wide: ~836 ha damaged (natural forest ~676 ha, plantations ~160 ha), ~118,100 m3; mean damaged-area fraction ~32 %; worst on ridges and plateaus in the west
effect_on_stand: partial canopy loss; damage at the tower stand itself not quantified
citation: Hiura T., Okuda A., Okuyama S., Hino T. (2005) 苫小牧研究林における2004年18号台風の被害と今後の課題 (Damage by Typhoon No. 18 of 2004 in the Tomakomai Experimental Forest and future issues). 北方森林保全技術 (Tech. Rep. Boreal For. Conserv., Hokkaido Univ. Forests) 23:24-26
quote: 森林被害実面積は天然林で約676ha、人工林で約160ha、計約836haに及んだ。
note: Translation: 'actual forest damage area reached about 676 ha of natural forest and about 160 ha of plantation, about 836 ha in total.' Same section: damaged-area ratio 'averaged about 32 %' (平均で約32％). Not tower-specific.

extent_or_severity: 20 m flux tower tilted; instruments removed; new tower installed the next spring
effect_on_stand: flux record gap and possible footprint change after spring 2005
citation: Hiura T., Okuda A., Okuyama S., Hino T. (2005) 苫小牧研究林における2004年18号台風の被害と今後の課題 (Damage by Typhoon No. 18 of 2004 in the Tomakomai Experimental Forest and future issues). 北方森林保全技術 (Tech. Rep. Boreal For. Conserv., Hokkaido Univ. Forests) 23:24-26
quote: 炭素フラックス観測を継続して行ってきた20ｍタワーが傾いたため各種測器を回収し、翌春新たなタワーを設置して台風被害後の炭素フラックスの観測を再開した。
note: Translation: 'the 20 m tower used for continuous carbon-flux observation tilted, so the instruments were recovered; a new tower was installed the following spring and carbon-flux observation resumed after the typhoon damage.' Supports the BADM two-tower record (first tower ending 2004-09-08). Month of the new tower ('next spring') is approximate.

extent_or_severity: removal of fallen trees blocking forest roads (~1.5 months for main roads, ~1 more month in spring 2005)
effect_on_stand: road clearing only; root-lifted trees fell during winter 2004-05
citation: Hiura T., Okuda A., Okuyama S., Hino T. (2005) 苫小牧研究林における2004年18号台風の被害と今後の課題 (Damage by Typhoon No. 18 of 2004 in the Tomakomai Experimental Forest and future issues). 北方森林保全技術 (Tech. Rep. Boreal For. Conserv., Hokkaido Univ. Forests) 23:24-26
quote: 台風によって倒れはしなかったが根が浮いた状態となった樹木が積雪や季節風の影響で冬期間に倒れ
note: Translation: 'trees not toppled by the typhoon but left with lifted roots fell during winter under snow and seasonal wind.' Delayed mortality after the typhoon; no stand-level salvage reported. Not tower-specific.

extent_or_severity: landscape-scale; ground largely bare until the early 20th century
effect_on_stand: near-zero soil carbon accumulation before reforestation (RothC assumes no soil C in 1900)
citation: Kominami Y., Jomura M., Dannoura M., Goto Y., Tamai K., Miyama T., Kanazawa Y., Kaneko S., Okumura M., Misawa N., Hamada S., Sasaki T., Kimura H., Ohtani Y. (2008) Biometric and eddy-covariance-based estimates of carbon balance for a warm-temperate mixed forest in Japan. Agric. For. Meteorol. 148:723-737
quote: Since the 6th century, the forests around the study site have been harvested heavily and then abandoned, leaving much of the ground bare until the early 20th century.
note: Historic over-harvest / bare hills (suburban forest use). FFPRI Japanese page: the area was bare from use as a suburban forest.

extent_or_severity: broad-scale reforestation
effect_on_stand: Pinus densiflora forest established
citation: Kominami Y., Jomura M., Dannoura M., Goto Y., Tamai K., Miyama T., Kanazawa Y., Kaneko S., Okumura M., Misawa N., Hamada S., Sasaki T., Kimura H., Ohtani Y. (2008) Biometric and eddy-covariance-based estimates of carbon balance for a warm-temperate mixed forest in Japan. Agric. For. Meteorol. 148:723-737
quote: During the early 1900s, an extensive reforestation effort using P. densiflora was carried out. This was the first broad-scale revegetation work in Japan in modern times.
note: FFPRI Japanese page: greening works begun about 100 years ago by de Rijke (デレーケ). Pine establishment year 1900 is the paper's tree-ring based assumption.

effect_on_stand: Quercus serrata and Ilex pedunculosa invade under the pines and later become the canopy
citation: Kominami Y., Jomura M., Dannoura M., Goto Y., Tamai K., Miyama T., Kanazawa Y., Kaneko S., Okumura M., Misawa N., Hamada S., Sasaki T., Kimura H., Ohtani Y. (2008) Biometric and eddy-covariance-based estimates of carbon balance for a warm-temperate mixed forest in Japan. Agric. For. Meteorol. 148:723-737
quote: Broadleaved species such as Q. serrata and evergreen species as I. pedunculosa that had invaded the site during the 1950s gradually became the dominant canopy species.
note: Natural broadleaf regeneration; establishment c. 1960 per tree rings.

extent_or_severity: most Pinus densiflora killed; pine now 6 % of living biomass (1999)
effect_on_stand: shift to oak-dominated secondary forest; large pine CWD legacy (dead pine 6.79 MgC ha-1)
citation: Kominami Y., Jomura M., Dannoura M., Goto Y., Tamai K., Miyama T., Kanazawa Y., Kaneko S., Okumura M., Misawa N., Hamada S., Sasaki T., Kimura H., Ohtani Y. (2008) Biometric and eddy-covariance-based estimates of carbon balance for a warm-temperate mixed forest in Japan. Agric. For. Meteorol. 148:723-737
quote: However, between about 1975 and 1984, most of these trees were killed by the pine wilt disease.
note: RothC run assumed peak mortality 1975-1984 at 20x background rate. FFPRI page: 'After the invasion by pine wilt disease in 1980's, Konara oak has taken over'.

extent_or_severity: about 10 % of total biomass died 2015-2016
effect_on_stand: Quercus serrata mortality from oak wilt (Platypus quercivorus); summer NEP turned negative in 2015; shift toward evergreen Quercus glauca expected
citation: Yamanoi K., Mizoguchi Y., Fukayama T., Takanashi S., Yasuda Y., Kominami Y., Kitamura K., Miyata A., Kim W., Ono K., Murayama S., Maeda T., Ishidoya S., Saigusa N., Takahashi Y. (FY2012-2016 final report) Sensor-network and automated analysis for refined monitoring of terrestrial carbon cycle variation, (1) high-precision observation system [Japanese]. Ministry of the Environment, Japan
quote: 2015年から、現在拡大中のカシノナガキクイムシによるコナラ枯死被害が発生し、全バイオマスの約10%が2015年から2016年にかけて枯死した。
note: Translation: 'From 2015, Quercus serrata die-off caused by the spreading oak ambrosia beetle (kashinaga-kikuimushi) occurred; about 10 % of total biomass died in 2015-2016.' Same page: Yasso model predicts the NEP minimum in 2018-2019 and an effect lasting about 20 yr. Contradicts the site plan 'No composition change documented' for 2000-2023: evaluate 2015 onward separately.

extent_or_severity: most red pines killed
effect_on_stand: replacement by ~60-yr Quercus serrata / Ilex pedunculosa secondary forest
citation: Yamanoi K., Mizoguchi Y., Yasuda Y., Ohtani Y., Nakai Y., Kitamura K., Takanashi S., Kominami Y., Fukayama T., Hagino H., Miyata A., Mano M., Ono K., Kondo H., Murayama S., Maeda T., Ishidoya S., Saigusa N., Takahashi Y. (FY2007-2011 final report) Long-term ecosystem monitoring for Asian terrestrial carbon-cycle observation and data networking, (1) monitoring sites and standardised observation systems [Japanese]. Ministry of the Environment, Japan, Global Environment Research Fund
quote: 1900～1910年にかけて緑化工事によりアカマツ林が形成され、その後、1970年代後半にマツ枯れによってほとんどのアカマツが枯死
note: Translation: 'red pine forest was formed by greening works in 1900-1910; then in the late 1970s most red pines died of pine wilt.' Dates as 'late 1970s'; Kominami et al. 2008 give peak mortality 1975-1984; the BIF says 1980s.
